Inhabited.CharacterDef.label: High Marshal Wenna Dask
Inhabited.CharacterDef.childhood: fourth of seven on a holding that ran three vaporators and needed five.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.adult: elected High Marshal four times by people who have never once done what she asked.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.hook: Sun-cracked, sixty kilos, and a voice like a kettle just before it goes — and her entire method of government is asking, out loud, twice, and then standing there until it is embarrassing. Nobody refuses her, because refusing takes longer than agreeing. She has no power to make one household help another, and she has watched two families starve out eleven kilometres from full cisterns, and she still will not take an authority she was not given.

Inhabited.CharacterDef.label: Ord Halloway
Inhabited.CharacterDef.childhood: raised on the rule and made to recite it before he could work a valve.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.adult: gave a Tusken scout water at his own trough, in the spring of the bad year.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.hook: Hands like split leather and a face that has never once been pleased about anything. The band came back in the autumn and took his elder son and four vaporators — and his trough is still outside his fence, still full, still unwatched. Say one admiring word about that and he will run you off his ground swearing. He is not being humble. He thinks praise turns a rule into a favour, and a favour is a thing that can be withdrawn.

Inhabited.CharacterDef.label: Vekshaa
Inhabited.CharacterDef.childhood: came off a freighter at nineteen with a salt habit and no way home.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.adult: drinks. That is the entire occupation. No one in the Covenant may refuse him.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.hook: Horned, and his hide has gone from red-brown to a dull ashy grey after eleven years of salt — his people are desert-born and he needs four times the water a man does *because* of the salt and cannot stop taking the salt. He is the most grateful person on the terminator — thanks you by name, warmly, every single time, and means it. He has drunk two holdings down to the sludge and moved on, and both of them let him, because the well belongs to whoever is thirsty standing at it, and he is always thirsty, and he is always standing at it.

Inhabited.CharacterDef.label: Onk-Onk-Deshu
Inhabited.CharacterDef.childhood: unrecorded, and if you ask her she will still be answering at sundown.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.adult: stands in the north field. Has stood there, broadly speaking, for six years.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.hook: Vast, slow, three hundred kilos of patient bulk that newcomers hitch animals to. She takes about four seconds a word and keeps her own hide damp from the inside — a low wet drone you feel through the floor — and she needs no well at all, ever, which is a problem nobody in the Covenant of Free Wells has worked out what to do with. ⭐ She is also the only Hutt on the terminator who has never wanted anything from anybody, which the Cartel finds more offensive than a debt. She pays into the trough fund anyway. No one has heard the end of one of her sentences, so she is widely held to be the wisest person in Bell Cistern.

Inhabited.CharacterDef.label: Pell Onasso
Inhabited.CharacterDef.childhood: herded before he could talk. Both mouths, and every word of both, on the animals.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.adult: runs four hundred head on water Bell Cistern cannot spare and will not cull one.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.hook: A long curved head and two mouths that fall silent at different moments, and he has named every animal he owns and grieves each one aloud, in stereo, for a week. He will not put down a lame beast — not for meat, not for water, not for mercy — so a third of the herd is old cripples and it drinks like a second settlement. Admire somebody else's stock in front of him and he goes silent for a day and a half. Bell Cistern has voted on this twice and both times concluded it was his ground and none of their business.

Inhabited.CharacterDef.label: Uzzo One-Eye
Inhabited.CharacterDef.childhood: nomad-raised under a custom that says the suffering are helped out of it.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.adult: twenty years on the Bell Cistern water gang. Lost the eye in his first season and did not slow down.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.hook: One eye — the other went to a well collapse before most of the gang was born — an arm rebuilt out of parts that were somebody else's, and a hide that lets him work a full shift in the open at noon, which nobody else here can do. He is the gentlest man in the settlement, and he will still — sincerely, quietly, kindly — offer to end anyone in real pain, the old, the crushed, the dying, and be genuinely wounded by how they take it. He has been told. He has been told for twenty years. It will not stay in.

Inhabited.CharacterDef.label: Marda Ilk
Inhabited.CharacterDef.childhood: taken from Marrowfield at nine. Raised in the Sun-Debt. Adopted properly, with a name.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.adult: walked back in at twenty-two. Keeps vaporators for a living.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.hook: She has not shown her face to another person in twenty-five years and will not, so she eats alone in a shed, every meal, and has stopped being asked. She keeps eleven vaporators beautifully and apologises to the air each time one fills, because the water was taken and a debt is a debt. She is the only person in the League who could talk to a raiding party, and the League will not permit it — a League seen talking is a League seen paying — and she thinks that is the stupidest thing she has ever heard and says so, at length, to anyone.

Inhabited.CharacterDef.label: Captain Duro Vensk
Inhabited.CharacterDef.childhood: read every campaign history the Stillmarket peddlers ever carried in.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.adult: commands the Bell Cistern militia, which has never in its existence gone anywhere.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.hook: Tall, dry, immaculate, and under his bed is a chest holding nineteen plans for the destruction of the deep desert wells — worked out to the canteen, each one dated, and any of them would work. He shows them to visitors. He will never execute one and does not want to, because *we stand on our own ground* — and he is so proud of not doing it that he has brought it up at two other people's funerals.

Inhabited.CharacterDef.label: Hobb Merrit
Inhabited.CharacterDef.childhood: nothing happened, and he can date it.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.adult: won a boundary arbitration eleven years ago. Entirely. On every point.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.hook: He won. He got the strip, he got the trough rights, he got the apology in writing, and he has not stopped for eleven years — the whole thing in order, with the wording, in a voice like a shovel going into gravel, forty minutes, still furious. Barrin Toke, who lost, lives nine hundred metres east. When Toke's condenser failed last winter Hobb hauled him water for nine days unasked and without one word, then came home and told the story again.

Inhabited.CharacterDef.label: Kkit-Nabb
Inhabited.CharacterDef.childhood: five hems, two of which he sold.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.adult: took the Covenant at twenty-four. The only Jawa ever to do it, as far as anyone knows.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.hook: Two glowing eyes at chest height, a smell that arrives well ahead of him, and a chatter like a saw blade dropped on stone. He will steal anything you own — parts, boots, the pin out of your hinge — and regards that as evidence of his good character. He will not touch water. He once walked eleven kilometres in the dark, both ways, to put a canteen back where he found it, told nobody, and has been insufferable about the Covenant to his own clan ever since, who find the entire business obscene.

Inhabited.CharacterDef.label: Bessa Trull
Inhabited.CharacterDef.childhood: taught that a debt you did not agree to is still a debt.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.adult: her aquifer went brackish four years ago. Stillmarket has hauled her water free since.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.hook: Wire-thin and going grey at forty-four, and the most generous person in this town toward anybody except herself. She will not take the haulage as a gift, so she works it off — at night, after her own day, on other people's ground — and she is thirty-one months ahead of anything anyone claims she owes. They have stopped telling her. She is starting to look like something left out in the sun, and if you say so she will thank you for your concern and add a shift.

Inhabited.CharacterDef.label: Sev'ka Dorn
Inhabited.CharacterDef.childhood: raised on the assumption that everything worth having is taken quietly.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.adult: runs an intelligence and influence network inside a market town of four hundred people.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.hook: Fur that ripples visibly when he lies — he has been told this, by everyone, for nine years — and a habit of breathing through his mouth when he is close to something he wants. He keeps files. He has leverage on eleven households and a whisper campaign running against a man who does not know he exists. It achieves nothing whatsoever: there is no office to capture, nobody obeys anybody, and the High Marshal cannot make you do a thing. He has never once suspected the problem is structural.

Inhabited.CharacterDef.label: Arda Fenn
Inhabited.CharacterDef.childhood: watched a stranger drink at her father's trough and ride off with three of his animals.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.adult: has argued against the free-well rule at every Stillmarket gathering for thirty-one years.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.hook: A voice like a hinge being forced and an argument that is, irritatingly, rather good — the rule is a subsidy paid by the poorest holdings to the worst people alive, and she has the figures, by year, and will read them. She has never broken it once. She hands you the cup while telling you the cup is going to kill us all. Nobody will call a vote on it, because calling a vote implies somebody could be *bound* by one, and that is the other thing she cannot get a single person here to see.

Inhabited.CharacterDef.label: Hoggo Bar-Tesh
Inhabited.CharacterDef.childhood: born owned. Kajidic property, third generation, in the pits at eleven.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.adult: bought out, bought in, and is the only trader in Stillmarket who deals with Hutt factors.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.hook: Horned, leather-hided, permanently cheerful, and he does brisk, scrupulously honest business with the people who owned his mother, because he has decided the way to stop being a thing is to become a price. He carries no gun — a gun is what a frightened man buys — and he has put two men through a stall front with his hands this year. The town is quietly sick about the trading and buys from him anyway, because he is the best there is.

Inhabited.CharacterDef.label: Wenn Kaddo
Inhabited.CharacterDef.childhood: unremarkable, in a family of eight who all remember it the same way.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.adult: attends. Every arbitration, gathering, funeral and dispute. Eighteen years.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.hook: He stands at the back, and you notice him because of the breathing — a slow wet catch on the intake that fills every pause in the room. He has no stake in one single matter, has never spoken at one, and does not repeat a word of what he hears, ever, to anyone, which has been tested twice. He simply likes being in the room. Stillmarket has decided this is fine. Nobody is entirely comfortable, and nobody can name what they would be entitled to object to.

Inhabited.CharacterDef.label: Ilva Prute
Inhabited.CharacterDef.childhood: heard the silence at eleven and has been explaining it ever since.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.adult: the Covenant has no priests. She is one anyway, and stopping her would require an authority.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.hook: She preaches at the Stillmarket trough every dawn in a carrying nasal blare audible from the far side of the market, and the drinkers stand and take it, politely, and have for eleven years. The sermon is not the problem. The problem is that when she is moved she pours water over people's heads — strangers, unasked, a full dipper — and pouring water onto the ground is the nearest thing this faith has to blasphemy, and she does it out of love, and there is no rule against it because nobody imagined anyone would.

Inhabited.CharacterDef.label: Nessa Halloway
Inhabited.CharacterDef.childhood: Ord Halloway's granddaughter. Was six the autumn the band came.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.hook: She has announced she is leaving this planet — to everyone, repeatedly — and the entire settlement is helping her do it. The Marshal found her the routes, the peddlers are teaching her script and Huttese, four households are putting money by for the passage, because a person belongs to herself and going is not a betrayal. She is delighted. She is also furiously, secretly insulted that not one of them has asked her to stay, and she has begun saying cruel and extremely accurate things to the people packing her bag.

Inhabited.CharacterDef.label: Tessa Vorn
Inhabited.CharacterDef.childhood: apprenticed to a well-digger and better at it than him by fifteen.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.adult: fought the outside well for two years, lost the vote, and has maintained it alone since.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.hook: She argued for two years that putting the trough beyond the wall would get people killed, and she was very probably right, and she lost. She now keeps it in better order than anything else in the holding — lined, shaded, scrubbed weekly, at her own cost, on her own time. She will stand at it and tell you in detail exactly why it should not be there. She will also break the arm of anyone she catches fouling it, and has.

Inhabited.CharacterDef.label: Emm Dorrow
Inhabited.CharacterDef.childhood: youngest of the Dorrows, and the one whose chest was never right.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.adult: farms the eastern edge. Has not been raided in nine years.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.hook: A soft, breathless, apologetic man who fills a forty-litre cistern every month and carries it out to a marker stone at the lip of the Scorch — alone, at night, in four stages, because he cannot manage it in one. Everyone in Marrowfield knows. Nobody will say it aloud, because said aloud it is tribute and a free man does not pay tribute, so it is nothing, and he does it, and the holding stands. He has started leaving more than water. Last month it was a crate of medicine.

Inhabited.CharacterDef.label: Ovett Sarn
Inhabited.CharacterDef.childhood: her mother made the first six of them out of a condenser housing.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.adult: has built two hundred and eleven guns out of vaporator scrap and can name who holds each.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.hook: Hands like bird bones — she cannot lift a full can and has to be helped onto her own stool — and every weapon in this holding came off her bench. They are bad guns. She knows precisely how bad and cannot do better with what there is. What she cannot bear is anyone else touching one: she has taken her own work off a grown man in the road, in front of people, to clean a scratch, and handed it back an hour later without a word about it.

Inhabited.CharacterDef.label: Cabba Ressik
Inhabited.CharacterDef.childhood: nothing. She was elsewhere.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.adult: sorts and bales fodder. Has never in her life been present when anything happened.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.hook: She arrived after. She always arrives after — the raid, the collapse, the wedding, the argument — and she knows everyone who was there, and she will give you the whole thing accurately in a flat honking drone, crediting who told her which part, for as long as you stand still. Marrowfield uses her as an index and has never told her that is what she is for. Nothing has ever happened to her. She does not appear to mind and does not appear to have noticed.

Inhabited.CharacterDef.label: Ren Ashek
Inhabited.CharacterDef.childhood: perfectly ordinary, in a house that loved her and got nothing back.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.adult: sits with the dying. Volunteered. Argued for the job on the merits and won the argument.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.hook: She feels nothing, and has said so plainly at a gathering, to four hundred people, and made the case that this is exactly why the job should be hers — and Marrowfield are libertarians and could not fault the reasoning. She keeps a card with the correct things to say written on it and reads from it openly, at the bedside, in front of the family. The dying find it enormously comforting. Somebody wrote it down. Somebody sat and worked out what would help, and then came.

Inhabited.CharacterDef.label: Old Sannit
Inhabited.CharacterDef.childhood: fifty-one years of it, by his own reckoning, which is not reliable.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.adult: Marrowfield's arbiter, by unanimous consent of every party to every dispute.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.hook: There are no courts and no judges here, so a matter goes to whoever both sides will accept, and both sides always accept Sannit, because he is the only man in the holding who has never wanted anything. He is also drunk from about the second hour. He hears the whole case sober, in the morning, perfectly, and forgets nothing — then delivers at dusk, slurring, sometimes weeping. The rulings bind because everybody agreed in advance that they would, and nobody has ever proposed moving the hour.

Inhabited.CharacterDef.label: Tam Orrel
Inhabited.CharacterDef.childhood: the handsomest child anyone here had seen, and told so daily from the age of two.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.adult: holds six unpaid Marrowfield posts. Is bad at all six.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.hook: He is genuinely magnificent to look at and people simply vote for him, over and over, for every position the holding bothers to fill — water rota, fodder audit, storm watch — and he accepts every one because refusing would be rude, and then loses the paperwork. He eats constantly and enormously and it has not touched him yet. He is not vain, not exactly stupid, and nowhere near up to it, and the entire administration of Marrowfield is his to ruin because nobody could think of a fair reason to stop him.

Inhabited.CharacterDef.label: Halla Vetch
Inhabited.CharacterDef.childhood: took a lungful of grit at sixteen, in the storm that buried Old Marrowfield.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.adult: night watch on the desert side. Eleven years. Alone, by choice.
Inhabited.CharacterDef.hook: A scavenged rebreather that clicks twice on every exhale, so the whole wall always knows where she is. In eleven years she has never once raised the alarm — not because nothing comes, but because she has watched them come, drink, and go, and has concluded that this is what a free well is *for*. She reports it afterwards, in full, truthfully, every time, and lets the holding do as it likes with that. Marrowfield has argued about removing her for nine years. She would go the day they asked. Nobody has asked.
